subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:
I'm planning a young giraffe model facing +Z with a height around 2.6 meters, laying out the skeleton hierarchy from a central body root through spine, neck, head, jaw, tail, legs, and ears.

I'm positioning body parts with specific coordinates—front and hind legs, neck curve from shoulder to head, with ossicones bringing total height near 2.85 meters—then working out the coat coloring using patch-based textures with a cream base and chestnut tones, plus a gradient fade for the legs.

Working out color blending logic...

Defining spine and neck joint chains...

Still building head geometry...

Adding white eye highlights and small fanned lashes above each eye. For the ears, I'm planning big leaf-shaped flattened sphere scales positioned outward and upward at the sides of the head, with paler pink inner-ear detail nested inside.

Making the ear thin along z so the plate faces forward like a giraffe's sideways ear, with a smaller pale inner sphere offset slightly. Now I'm placing ossicones at the skull top, as thin rods angled up and back with skin-colored sweeps, topped with small black tufted spheres to suggest the fuzzy tips.

Still building ossicone and mane details...

Doubling the mane spikes with slight sideways offsets, then planning the tail as a tapering swept chain of catmull points from the croup down to a thin tan tip.

Adding a black tuft capsule and sphere at the tail's end, and setting up a root joint so the spine and tail chains have a proper shared parent. Now I'm sketching the front leg rig with hip, knee, fetlock, and hoof joint positions for a straight-standing rest pose.

Adding leg thickness tapering with knee and fetlock bumps...

Mapping out the hind leg path with the angled hock, then shaping the spine curve so the withers sit higher than the rump, giving the body that sloping giraffe silhouette with rounder radius near the rump.

Working out the neck taper now, narrowing the radius from base to tip while keeping it laterally slimmer than tall, and figuring out how the neck's forward lean affects the mane's orientation along the dorsal line.

For the head, I'll keep it simple with a tan skull color, a lighter muzzle tone, and dark nostril accents, assigning everything to a head bone and joint rather than overcomplicating with extra facial patterns.

The head joint connects to the end of the neck chain at roughly (0,2.45,0.97), with the skull sphere centered just above so the neck tucks neatly into the back of the skull given their respective radii. Then I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head for the lower jaw capsule.

Building the muzzle and jaw capsules so the mouth sits closed, then adding a small tongue capsule with a tip sphere that peeks slightly below the front of the muzzle for a natural touch.

Now I'm placing the eyes as bulging spheres on the skull, sizing them against the skull's width at that height, and adding tiny white highlight spheres positioned outward and forward for a glint before working on the lashes.

Adding lash rods...

Then I'm adding a darker socket ring behind each eye and small dark nostril spheres on the nose.

For ossicones, I'm building tapered rods from base to tip with skin-colored fuzz, topped with a dark tufted sphere and radial spikes for texture.

Now I'm setting up joint names across the body: ossicone bones, ear joints, and bilateral leg chains using a left/right side loop, naming shoulder, knee, wrist, and fetlock joints for front legs so the rigger recognizes standard conventions.

I'm defining the hind-leg chain names (hip, hock, fetlock, hoof) to avoid collisions with front-leg names, plus setting up spine, neck, and tail chains with the right number of joints and spans, including binding the tail's black tuft bone to the last tail joint.

Now I'm figuring out which chain joint index corresponds to the knee, fetlock, and hoof spheres so the leg bends correctly, then checking floor placement — making sure the hoof cylinder bottom sits exactly at y=0 and the leg tube reaches just inside it. I'm also double-checking that the tail tuft ends at a sensible height and that the total figure height, including the ossicone tip and tuft, looks proportional for a young giraffe.

Now I'm defining the color palette (cream base, reddish-brown chest patches) and setting up the patch-mixing and painting functions, along with the mane construction using a sweep along the neck and spike elements for texture.

Finalizing the root export and skipping extra body details like tuft or hip bumps, focusing instead on a radius function that tapers the body shape smoothly along its length.
